correctness.rationale: Exact polynomial factorizations give two maps reducing to ±t modulo 3 and hence isometric bijections at every power. The third branch has the verified identity F(3t)=3/128+3w²(9w²-10)/128 with w=2t-1; its unit factor is 1 modulo 3 and is absorbed by a bijective square-root coordinate change. This gives every fiber as 2+3 times an exact modular square-root count and proves least period 3^(k+1). Root multiplicity classification and normalized Haar measure follow from valuations. Direct exact-integer enumeration and a standalone checker corroborate k=1..7, without replacing proof. The branch hypotheses are for all t∈Z3, all k≥1.

value.rationale: The fourth binomial-column residues are a classical natural integer sequence; the 3-adic value fiber distribution is an exact arithmetical invariant. The least-period and all-residue surjectivity hold despite a singular third input branch, which creates a nonuniform infinite hierarchy of fiber sizes and an exceptional image set of Haar measure 1/8. This is a complete classification at the smallest excluded odd prime of a closely motivated same-object prime-power value-set problem, not an arbitrary finite slice or a restatement of basic square counting.
